title: Japan Travel Advice
body:
O.P.
this post was edited
Continues from: /forum-replies.cfm?t=2642614&p=-1#bottom
As per A777 (#101222) advice in previous Opening Threads:
If you are asking for advice on itinerary or accommodation and you have exact dates then please post the EXACT DATES including days of the week
Upcoming events include the autumn colours and then of course winter, winter festivals, winter illuminations, skiing, snowboarding and snowy onsen!
Seasons make a big difference in Japan. Weekends make a big difference. Public holidays make a big difference. Day of the month can make a difference as most religious/temple related events are date related and they don't move just because it is/isn't on a weekend. Day of the week can make a big difference as many museums shut on Mondays for example.
Accommodation pricing can also triple during peak times.
Also, if you know your flight arrival and departure times then please post these and the airports. Tokyo is not sufficient, specify Haneda or Narita.
Discussion on flight sales and pricing is in the Flights to Japan thread:- /forum-replies.cfm?t=1948442
My preferred format for itineraries is day by day including date and day of the week :- Thu 18 Aug 2016 ... Fri 19 Aug ... Sat 20 Aug Sun 21 Aug etc.
And of course, read the FAQ.
Thank you!!

Looking for suggestions here. I am researching Ginza, Roppongi and Asakusa. In my previous visit, I have done the high level stuff – Shinjuku, Shibuya. Harajuku, Ueno/Ameyoko, Akihabara, Tsukiji Fish Market. My accommodation is in Shibuya.
Ginza – look at the high end shops in general (not necessarily shopping!), try Ramen St (Rokinshura ramen) Roppongi – look at surrounding areas, perhaps Roppongi Hills and I understand this place cater more for nightlife (I am not into clubbing but friend suggested to go night time)? Asakusa – Nakamise St, Sensoji temple, Kappabashi St (wife loves kitchen stuff)
Looking at google maps, Ginza and Roppongi are quite close to each other while Asakusa is slightly a bit way off. Should I tackle Asakusa first, then Ginza and finally go to Roppongi to see what it can offer at night? Possible in one day? Or should I spread it over two days? Any food suggestion around this area? Thanks!
[User #4008798711 postsdtcrefreshes my brainWhirlpool Forums Addict] kc01 writes...
Should I tackle Asakusa first, then Ginza and finally go to Roppongi to see what it can offer at night? Possible in one day?
That seems logical. Keep in mind that many shops don’t open until 11 or 12. So Sensoji first, maybe 930/10 ish (unless you want to avoid the crowds, in which case earlier – but then the stalls won’t be open), then wander around Asakusa and up to Kappabashi St. Then over to Ginza (Ginza line from tawaramachi) and then roppongi (hibiya Line).

[User #5673511237 postsOrangeKnightotakuWhirlpool Enthusiast] this post was edited
Just quick question. I want to visit Fushimi Inari shrine but I don't like crowds. Should I visit the shrine early in the morning or in the afternoon/evening? Also Fushimi Inari and Arashiyama in one day is doable? I known Fushimi Inari is in the North East and Arashiyama is on the South but I don't have other days left for Kyoto.
Here's my itinerary (which I posted on the previous thread):
January 14 (Sunday) : Arrive at Tokyo at 5am, leave luggage at hotel. Visit Meiji shrine, Harajuku then Shibuya. Check in at hotel before dinner. January 15 (Monday) : Half day Tokyo tour. (Tour includes Tokyo Tower, Imperial Palace, Asakua and Ends at Tokyo station. Tokyo Skytree then go back to Marunouchi to exchange the JR Pass voucher and book for shinkansen tickets. Explor the shops in Ginza and Mrunouchi until night then return to hotel after dinner. January 16 (Tuesday) : Activate 7 day JR Pass, travel to Himeji (I just want to see the castle), stroll around then travel to Hiroshima and check in at hotel. I might visit the A bomb dome and museum if there is still time. January 17 (Wednesday) : Mazda museum tour (english) in the morning. Then head to Miyajima until dusk. Go back to hotel after dinner. January 18 (Thursday) : travel to Kyoto. Explore central Kyoto then go back to hotel after dinner. January 19 (Friday) : Explore eastern Kyoto for the day. Kiyomizudera, Ginkakuji, Higashiyama, Gion. Return to hotel after dinner. January 20 (Saturday) : Fushimi Inari Shrine. Maybe half day then other half will be in the Arashiyama district. Go back to hotel after dinner. January 21 (Sunday) : Travel to Kanazawa from Kyoto. Explore Kanazawa before going back to hotel after dinner. January 22 (Monday) : Travel to Shirakawago in the morning after check out. Travel back to Tokyo before dinner. January 23 (Tuesday) : Akihabara shopping, maid cafe (I love them), play arcades, Gachapons, AKB theatre (if I will score a ticket). January 24 (Wednesday) : Ghibli Museum. Odaiba for the Gundam and Rainbow bridge in the evening. January 25 (Thursday) : check out at hotel then last minute shopping in Akihabara before heading to airport for 10pm departure. January 26 (Friday) : Arrive in Melbourne.
Hotels: 2 nights at Courtyard by Marriott Tokyo Station 2 nights at Hotel Granvia Hiroshima 3 nights at New Miyako Hotel Kyoto 1 night at HOTEL MYSTAYS Kanazawa Castle 3 nights at REMM Akihabara hotel

[User #640018286 poststt7Forum Regular] OrangeKnight writes...
Just quick question. I want to visit Fushimi Inari shrine but I don't like crowds. Should I visit the shrine early in the morning or in the afternoon/evening? Also Fushimi Inari and Arashiyama in one day is doable? I known Fushimi Inari is in the North East and Arashiyama is on the South but I don't have other days left for Kyoto.
Assuming Kyoto Station as the starting point, Fushimi Inari is south-south-east and Arashiyama is north-west (though that doesn’t really matter, just get a train from Kyoto Station).
Both are probably better done early in the morning, as early as you can. I’d go to Fushimi Inari first then head back to the station and get the train to Saga-Arashiyama. I assume you are going to the Bamboo Grove but would suggest also visiting Tenryu-ji and Okochi-Sanso. Tenryu-ji (which has a very nice garden) is between the station and the Grove, so could be done either on the way to the Grove or on the way back – you can exit (on the way to the Grove) or enter (on the way back) – Tenryu-ji via its north gate. When you get to the end of the Bamboo Grove, the entrance gate to Okochi-Sanso is ahead and to the right. Most people either miss it or don’t want to pay the ¥1,000 entrance fee but it’s well worth it – a very pleasant stroll garden and the entrance fee includes tea and a very nice biscuity thing in the teahouse afterwards.
If you start early enough, you can visit both by lunchtime, depending how far up the mountain you want to walk at Fushimi Inari. Tenryu-ji and Okochi-Sanso both open at 9 am (I think but check..).
